newsitem.title: USA: Consumer group protests Shell/Texaco merger.
newsitem.headline: Consumer group protests Shell/Texaco merger.

text.p: Consumer advocates Tuesday slammed the merger announced by Texaco Inc and Shell Oil Co of their Midwestern and Western U.S. refining and marketing operations.
"This merger will sharply reduce competition in major gasoline markets," said Edwin Rothschild, energy policy director for Citizen Action.
"The combination will result in just three companies in California--Arco, Chevron, and Texaco/Shell-- controlling over 75 percent of the gasoline market," he said.
Shell Oil is the U.S. subsidiary of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
"If allowed by the Federal Trade Commission, a merger between Shell and Texaco would set a dangerous precedent in the oil market," Rothschild said.
He said consumers were "fed up with industry whining about low profit margins" when over the long run, oil companies were highly profitable.
The new company, to be 56 percent owned by Shell and 44 percent owned by Texaco, will market gasoline under both company's brand names through independent wholesalers and retailers.
